creatures.name: Earth Caterpillar
creatures.flavor: Slow until it isn't.
creatures.lore: Slow until it isn't. In its final stage it accelerates without warning, drawing on something stored since it hatched. What it becomes afterward depends entirely on what it consumed.
creatures.death_flavor: The cocoon it never built still hangs, unfinished, in the bark.

creatures.name: Elder Centipede
creatures.flavor: It navigates by sensing the decay of other creatures.
creatures.lore: It navigates by sensing the decay of other creatures. Where something has died, it arrives — not to consume, but to remain. Over time, the places it has visited all look the same: older, darker, more alive.
creatures.death_flavor: The soil where it rested will be richer for years.

creatures.name: Moss Lizard
creatures.flavor: The first to arrive.
creatures.lore: The first to arrive. The last to leave. It has spent decades on the same log and the log has already grown around it.
creatures.death_flavor: Even now, the bark it rested on feels warm.

creatures.name: Peat Slug
creatures.flavor: Slower than the moss it lives on.
creatures.lore: Slower than the moss it lives on. It crosses the same stretch of root over several days, leaving a trail that other small things seem to follow. No one has studied where the trail goes.
creatures.death_flavor: The trail it left is still moist. Something is already using it.

creatures.name: Root Beetle
creatures.flavor: It spends most of its life underground, following root paths that have existed longer than the biome.
creatures.lore: It spends most of its life underground, following root paths that have existed longer than the biome. When it surfaces, it carries fragments of whatever it passed through.
creatures.death_flavor: The tunnel it dug still channels water three layers down.

creatures.name: Root Mycelium
creatures.flavor: It doesn't move.
creatures.lore: It doesn't move. It spreads. Given enough time, a single mycelium can thread its way through an entire section of root system without ever appearing above ground.
creatures.death_flavor: The network it built continues without it. Something else is already using the paths.

creatures.name: Stone Tortoise
creatures.flavor: No one has ever seen it move at speed.
creatures.lore: No one has ever seen it move at speed. It chooses its spot once, and that is enough. The moss on its shell is older than most of the trees nearby.
creatures.death_flavor: The hollow it left in the soil has already begun to fill with something green.

creatures.name: Ash Drake
creatures.flavor: Old for this biome — unheard of, really.
creatures.lore: Old for this biome — unheard of, really. It has outlasted every creature it shared the ash beds with. By the time it reaches its final stage, the rest of the ecosystem has cycled through several generations around it.
creatures.death_flavor: The heat it generated is already becoming something new.

creatures.name: Ash Salamander
creatures.flavor: Born from ember, it rarely lasts a season.
creatures.lore: Born from ember, it rarely lasts a season. But its children remember every mistake — and make new ones.
creatures.death_flavor: It burned bright. The ash it leaves still glows.

creatures.name: Ash Scorpion
creatures.flavor: Most ash creatures race through their lifecycle.
creatures.lore: Most ash creatures race through their lifecycle. The scorpion does not. It carries its venom carefully, as if saving it for something — though whatever that something is, it never arrives.
creatures.death_flavor: The mark its tail left in the ash will last until the next wind.

creatures.name: Char Mole
creatures.flavor: The only ash creature that goes deeper instead of faster.
creatures.lore: The only ash creature that goes deeper instead of faster. It digs into the carbon layers below the burn, into heat that hasn't changed in decades. Nobody knows what it is looking for down there.
creatures.death_flavor: The tunnel it dug collapsed slowly behind it.

creatures.name: Ember Falcon
creatures.flavor: It never lands.
creatures.lore: It never lands. From the moment it hatches it stays airborne, circling the thermals above the ash beds. When it finally comes down, that is the end.
creatures.death_flavor: The thermal it rode has already pulled something else upward.

creatures.name: Flame Wasp
creatures.flavor: Individually, inconsequential.
creatures.lore: Individually, inconsequential. In numbers, something that burns. It seems to know when it has company — the colony feeds and dies faster than any single creature would on its own.
creatures.death_flavor: Its stinger is still hot.

creatures.name: Smoke Serpent
creatures.flavor: Hard to see against the ashen ground.
creatures.lore: Hard to see against the ashen ground. It doesn't hunt so much as drift — arriving wherever warmth remains after a fire has passed. By the time the smoke clears, it is already gone.
creatures.death_flavor: The warmth where it coiled has already dissipated.

creatures.name: Crystal Dragonfly
creatures.flavor: Transparent from certain angles.
creatures.lore: Transparent from certain angles. From others, it refracts light into patterns on the ground below it. It isn't performing anything — that's simply what it is.
creatures.death_flavor: The refraction it left in the air persists for a moment, then finds its way to the ground.

creatures.name: Ethereal Butterfly
creatures.flavor: Its wings shouldn't keep it aloft.
creatures.lore: Its wings shouldn't keep it aloft. It loses altitude so slowly it barely registers — falling at all times, just sideways. It doesn't seem concerned about this.
creatures.death_flavor: The pollen it carried is already settling somewhere it will matter.

creatures.name: Mist Serpent
creatures.flavor: It prefers the space between stages — the moment after one thing ends and before the next begins.
creatures.lore: It prefers the space between stages — the moment after one thing ends and before the next begins. It has learned to extend those moments. Whether it does this consciously is unclear.
creatures.death_flavor: The mist it moved through briefly holds the shape of something passing.

creatures.name: Moon Moth
creatures.flavor: It only fully feeds at the slowest part of the night.
creatures.lore: It only fully feeds at the slowest part of the night. Patient in a way that feels less like waiting and more like knowing — as if it already knows the light will return and sees no reason to hurry toward it.
creatures.death_flavor: The scales it shed are still catching light that no longer exists.

creatures.name: Silk Spider
creatures.flavor: It builds continuously, even when there is nowhere left to build.
creatures.lore: It builds continuously, even when there is nowhere left to build. The web grows around itself, each generation adding another layer to something that was already complete.
creatures.death_flavor: The web it left will hold weight long after anyone remembers it built it.

creatures.name: Suspended Hummingbird
creatures.flavor: It moves constantly, but at high enough frequency that the effect is stillness.
creatures.lore: It moves constantly, but at high enough frequency that the effect is stillness. It has found a way to be in one place by never stopping moving. This seems exhausting. It does not appear exhausted.
creatures.death_flavor: The air where it hovered is still vibrating.

creatures.name: Veil Jellyfish
creatures.flavor: It drifts rather than swims.
creatures.lore: It drifts rather than swims. Where other creatures navigate, it simply adjusts — a slight tilt, a slow rotation — and ends up wherever the air currents decide.
creatures.death_flavor: The veil it trailed has already dispersed into something the rest of the garden can breathe.

creatures.name: Abyss Polyp
creatures.flavor: Anchored to the deepest point of the cave floor.
creatures.lore: Anchored to the deepest point of the cave floor. Where other fixed creatures simply endure, this one feeds — slowly, persistently, on whatever the dark brings past it.
creatures.death_flavor: The anchor point it held is already being colonised by something smaller.

creatures.name: Abyss Serpent
creatures.flavor: It comes from somewhere below the known cave.
creatures.lore: It comes from somewhere below the known cave. Its resource yield doesn't match its lifecycle length by any formula that works for other creatures. Something else is contributing.
creatures.death_flavor: For a moment after it dies, every other creature in the garden generates one final tick. Then the cave is quiet again.

creatures.name: Cave Scorpion
creatures.flavor: It doesn't move unless it has to.
creatures.lore: It doesn't move unless it has to. In the deep cave, not moving is a strategy — everything that found it first assumed it was stone. By the time they learned otherwise, it had already been there for years.
creatures.death_flavor: The depression it carved in the rock will outlast everything else in this record.

creatures.name: Crystal Crab
creatures.flavor: Its shell has grown around the quartz deposits it rests against.
creatures.lore: Its shell has grown around the quartz deposits it rests against. Removing it from its spot is theoretically possible. It would not be the same creature afterward.
creatures.death_flavor: The quartz where it rested is fractionally brighter than the surrounding rock.

creatures.name: Light Fish
creatures.flavor: It generates its own light, which it uses to navigate tunnels that have no other source.
creatures.lore: It generates its own light, which it uses to navigate tunnels that have no other source. Whether it needs the light to see or whether it simply prefers to illuminate what it passes through is not clear.
creatures.death_flavor: The tunnel it was in is darker than before it arrived.

creatures.name: Phosphor Eel
creatures.flavor: Leaves a trail of light as it moves.
creatures.lore: Leaves a trail of light as it moves. The trail fades in minutes, but while it lasts, other creatures seem to follow it — whether because of the light or in spite of it isn't certain.
creatures.death_flavor: The trail it left takes a little longer to fade than usual.

creatures.name: Quartz Snail
creatures.flavor: Each generation is slightly larger than the last.
creatures.lore: Each generation is slightly larger than the last. The shell it leaves becomes the base for the next. At this rate, in enough generations, the shell would be the largest thing in the cave. This is presumably fine.
creatures.death_flavor: The shell it left is already being filled with sediment from above.
